I am an environmental data scientist with the [Global Policy Lab](https://www.globalpolicy.science/) in the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability. Currently, we are researching urban development, land use transitions, and long-term impacts of protected areas in twentieth century sub-Saharan Africa by applying machine learning techniques to a digitized archive of 1.6 million historical aerial photos.

I earned my [Master of Environmental Data Science](https://bren.ucsb.edu/masters-programs/master-environmental-data-science) from the Bren School of Environmental Science & Management in 2025, and B.A.s in Political Science and Environmental Studies from UCSB in 2021. Before that, I worked at an environmental law firm specializing in Superfund remediation litigation, and spent years organizing local and federal campaigns rooted in social justice and conservation.

I grew up in [Palm Springs, CA](https://visitpalmsprings.com/), where summers get hot enough to melt the asphalt. Experiencing extreme heat as a child primed me to care about climate change early, and I am interested in questions about whether environmental or spatial factors shape our support for climate policies.

Outside of work, I enjoy cycling, quilting, and [photographing](photos.qmd) nature.

Recent work:

- Land cover change and protected area impact from a mega-archive of historical aerial imagery (in preparation)
- [Remote Sensing of Defensible Space Compliance to Enhance Wildfire Preparedness](https://bren.ucsb.edu/projects/remote-sensing-defensible-space-compliance-enhance-wildfire-preparedness) (Master's Capstone, 2025)
- [Santa Barbara County political mapping and voter registration analysis](posts/2025-03-17-voter-data-viz/SB-voter-visualization.qmd) (2025)
